executiveSummary.headline: Protect the Peer Lead While Improving Absolute Buyer Recognition
executiveSummary.lead: Fiesta Americana Condesa Cancún All Inclusive ranks first among four certified Fiesta Americana all-inclusive resort peers, yet absolute consideration is 2.8% and scenario presence is 11.1%. That combination is not evidence of a defect. The hotel already has recognized all-inclusive, beachfront, and spa strengths; the practical opportunity is to present under-recognized fitness, watersports, and romance attributes more clearly, while correcting public dining-count inconsistency and protecting the conditions attached to the airport-transfer offer.
executiveSummary.metricsNote: AI Consideration is based on 5 of 180 comparable monitored answers; Scenario Presence is based on 5 of 45 eligible scenarios. Certified Peer Position compares the four-hotel Fiesta Americana all-inclusive resort set. These measures do not represent bookings, revenue, or traveler exposure.

themes.title: Peer Leadership Does Not Equal Broad Consideration
themes.what: The resort is #1 of 4 in its certified peer set but appears in a small share of the broader monitored answers and scenarios.
themes.whyItMatters: The hotel can build on a relative strength while treating low absolute presence as a prioritization signal rather than a diagnosed website failure.

themes.title: Dining Inventory Needs One Count Language
themes.what: The official amenities page says 10 restaurants and bars, while Booking.com displays 15 restaurants.
themes.whyItMatters: The difference may reflect whether bars, counters, or seasonal outlets are counted. Guests and partners need one approved classification.

themes.title: Offer Conditions and Selective Differentiators Need Clarity
themes.what: Free airport transfer requires an official-site booking of at least four nights, while fitness, watersports, and honeymoon recognition remain partial.
themes.whyItMatters: Clear conditions prevent over-promising, and selective content can improve decision context without inventing defects or guaranteeing demand.

executiveSummary.successLooksLike: Official and priority partner pages use an approved restaurant-and-bar count; airport-transfer eligibility is stated consistently and prominently; verified fitness, watersports, Kids Club, Miiluma Spa, dog-friendly, and beachfront strengths are accurate; and leadership has made a documented romance-content decision.
executiveSummary.closing: The resort’s first-place peer rank is a sound foundation, not a reason to overstate performance. The best next step is disciplined information quality—align dining counts, protect offer conditions, and selectively strengthen real differentiators—then evaluate future movement through governed measurement. Digital authority: The resort’s strongest verified digital surfaces today are brand and major leisure-distribution pages. Digital content readiness: Condesa’s brand/all-inclusive pages and distributor listings create dining and transfer fact conflicts that matter more than backlink volume.

actionsResearchRecord.headline: Strengthen Under-Recognized Resort Differentiators
actionsResearchRecord.priorityWhy: The resort leads its certified peer set but has low absolute consideration and partial recognition of fitness and watersports.
actionsResearchRecord.whatWeFound: ADP recognized all-inclusive, beachfront, and spa strengths, while fitness was recognized in 24.6% and watersports in 16.9% of applicable observations. Kids Club, Miiluma Spa, dog-friendly positioning, and beachfront access are established strengths that must remain accurate.
actionsResearchRecord.whyItMatters: Clearer, well-organized facts can improve buyer decision context without inventing a defect or promising more AI mentions, bookings, or revenue.
recommendedSteps: Approve a concise resort differentiator fact sheet.
Clarify current fitness facilities, included versus paid watersports, Kids Club, Miiluma Spa, dog-friendly rules, and beachfront access.
Map approved facts across overview, amenities, FAQ, and priority partner listings.
Verify links, eligibility language, and live copy.
actionsResearchRecord.suggestedTimeframe: Brief in 2 weeks; approved updates within 30–45 days

completionCriteria.investigationCompleted: A signed differentiator sheet records current facts, inclusions, exclusions, and owners.
completionCriteria.correctionSubmitted: Approved content updates are filed for priority pages.
completionCriteria.correctionVerifiedLive: Live content matches the signed facts and retains working inquiry paths.
completionCriteria.noChangeRequired: Valid if leadership documents that current content already presents each prioritized differentiator accurately.

actionsResearchRecord.hotelApprovalNotes: Operations must confirm current availability, inclusions, restrictions, and seasonality.

changesOrInvestigation: Map approved differentiator facts to overview, amenities, FAQ, and supported metadata.
technicalDetails.verificationMethod: Compare rendered copy, FAQs, links, and available metadata against the signed fact sheet.
dependencies: Operations confirmation of current amenities and policies
technicalDetails.notes: Preserve already-recognized all-inclusive, beachfront, and spa strengths; do not overstate included activities.

actionsResearchRecord.headline: Align Restaurant and Bar Inventory Across Channels
actionsResearchRecord.priorityWhy: The official page and Booking.com publish different concrete dining counts.
actionsResearchRecord.whatWeFound: Official amenities copy says 10 restaurants and bars, while Booking.com lists 15 restaurants.
actionsResearchRecord.whyItMatters: Guests comparing channels should understand the actual outlet inventory and whether bars, counters, seasonal venues, or concepts are included.
recommendedSteps: Food and beverage signs a current outlet roster with type and operating status.
Define the counting rule for restaurants, bars, counters, and seasonal concepts.
Update official wording if needed and submit a field-level Booking.com correction.
Verify both pages and schedule recurring inventory review.
actionsResearchRecord.suggestedTimeframe: Source of truth in 2 weeks; partner correction within 30–45 days

completionCriteria.investigationCompleted: A signed outlet roster explains the official and Booking.com counts.
completionCriteria.correctionSubmitted: Approved official or Booking.com correction requests are filed.
completionCriteria.correctionVerifiedLive: Both pages match the signed roster and counting rule or open partner tickets are documented.
completionCriteria.noChangeRequired: Valid if both counts are correct under clearly explained, approved classifications and the public wording makes that distinction clear.

actionsResearchRecord.hotelApprovalNotes: Food and beverage leadership must approve the roster and counting rule before corrections.

changesOrInvestigation: Create a field-level roster and classify each venue by type and current operating status.
technicalDetails.verificationMethod: Compare live counts and named outlets against the signed roster and classification rule.
technicalDetails.notes: The mismatch is verified; the correct public count still requires hotel confirmation.

actionsResearchRecord.headline: Standardize Free Airport Transfer Conditions
actionsResearchRecord.priorityWhy: A valuable offer can be over-promised if the direct-booking, four-night, round-trip, and timing conditions are separated from the headline.
actionsResearchRecord.whatWeFound: Official pages state that transfer requires booking on the brand website for at least four nights; the offer page adds round-trip, package, and flight-information conditions.
actionsResearchRecord.whyItMatters: Consistent eligibility language reduces guest disappointment, call-center friction, and inaccurate summaries by travel partners or automated systems.
recommendedSteps: Revenue and reservations approve the complete current rule set.
Place a concise eligibility line beside every transfer headline.
Link property and amenities pages to the full offer terms.
QA booking confirmation, FAQ, call-center scripts, and partner descriptions.
actionsResearchRecord.suggestedTimeframe: Review in 2 weeks; approved updates within 30 days

completionCriteria.investigationCompleted: A signed offer sheet records eligibility, exclusions, booking steps, timing, and service owner.
completionCriteria.correctionSubmitted: Approved page, FAQ, and script updates are filed.
completionCriteria.correctionVerifiedLive: Every transfer headline has consistent eligibility language and a working full-terms link.
completionCriteria.noChangeRequired: Valid if all reviewed customer touchpoints already state the approved conditions clearly.

actionsResearchRecord.hotelApprovalNotes: Revenue and the brand offer owner must confirm current conditions before edits.

changesOrInvestigation: Compare headline, FAQ, full terms, booking confirmation, and call-center language.
technicalDetails.verificationMethod: Test links and compare every customer-facing condition against the signed offer sheet.
dependencies: Access to booking confirmation and call-center scripts
technicalDetails.notes: Do not imply that transfer is universal or available on hotel-plus-flight packages.

actionsResearchRecord.headline: Decide Whether to Expand Romance and Honeymoon Content
actionsResearchRecord.priorityWhy: Honeymoon recognition is partial, but more romance content is appropriate only if leadership wants and can serve that demand.
actionsResearchRecord.whatWeFound: ADP honeymoon recognition was 15.4%, and public guest context indicates couple interest. This does not establish a missing-page defect.
actionsResearchRecord.whyItMatters: A focused romance module could clarify fit and inquiry routing, but generic content would add maintenance and cannot guarantee leads or bookings.
recommendedSteps: Commercial leadership records a wedding/honeymoon go or no-go.
If go, define target occasions, packages, adult-versus-family positioning, proof points, and inquiry owner.
Draft concise content without weakening the family-resort proposition.
If no-go, document and close the action.
actionsResearchRecord.suggestedTimeframe: Decision within 30 days; content in 60–90 days if approved

completionCriteria.investigationCompleted: A written commercial go/no-go and target-segment rationale are on file.
completionCriteria.correctionSubmitted: If approved, a hotel-reviewed romance brief or page request is submitted.
completionCriteria.correctionVerifiedLive: If approved, live content matches confirmed packages and has a working inquiry path.
completionCriteria.noChangeRequired: Valid when leadership documents a no-go or confirms current romance content is sufficient.

actionsResearchRecord.hotelApprovalNotes: Optional opportunity; no additional wedding or honeymoon claim should publish without approved products and ownership.

supportingEvidence.note: Public couple-interest context; secondary source only.

dependencies: Confirmed romance products and operating owners
technicalDetails.notes: Optional commercial opportunity, not a verified defect.
